summary: Cross-tenant batch merging causing intermittent p95/p99 spikes and 504s in prod-us-east
description:
Issue summary:
BrightCart reports sudden intermittent tail latency (p95/p99) increases and a spike in 504 timeouts starting 2026-03-12 11:20 UTC in prod-us-east. The pattern correlates with times of heterogeneous tenant traffic bursts. Errors are transient but recurring (every 10-30 minutes) and last ~30-90s.

Impact:
- Customer-facing API calls for BrightCart degrade to p95 ~1.2s from baseline 300ms and p99 > 3s during events; 504s observed for ~0.5% of requests at peak.
- Affects multiple endpoints (chat generation + embedding endpoints) for the customer.
- Business impact: checkout recommendation widget timeouts, visible to end users.

Environment:
- prod-us-east (hosted, shared pool).
- Affected model flows: redwood-3b-1.0 for embeddings and meta-llama-7b for chat completions.

Steps to reproduce (customer test):
1) BrightCart sent a controlled replay of ~200 qps with mixed short/long sequences to prod-us-east at 2026-03-12T11:20Z.
2) Observe p95/p99 increase and occasional 504s in their traces.
3) When traffic is pinned to a dedicated pool for BrightCart, issue disappears.

Observed logs / metrics snippets:
- Serving-runtime logs show multiple batch ids where payloads from >=3 separate tenants were coalesced and the largest request in the batch increased per-token runtime by ~2.8x.
- Batcher metrics: batch_size distribution skews upward immediately before spikes; continuous-batcher window increases from baseline 8ms to 22-40ms during events.
- Router traces: a subset of requests show increased wait_time before being sent to runtime (wait_time correlates with batch assembly).
- Nginx upstream 504s align with last-mile request timeouts during long batch processing.

Hypothesis:
- Continuous batching is merging requests across tenants without respecting per-tenant request size heterogeneity, allowing a single long sequence to delay smaller requests in the same batch. Multi-tenant batch composition amplifies per-token execution time and causes head-of-line blocking.

Investigation notes so far:
- Replayed BrightCart traffic in staging with instrumentation: when tenant mixing allowed, median processing time per batch increased 1.9x and p99 latency reproduced.
- Verified KV-cache warmup not implicated: cache hit rates consistent across runs.
- Scheduler logs show batch assembly respects max_batch_size but not per-tenant max_seq_size heuristics.
- No recent deploys to serving-runtime between 2026-03-11 and incident start; routing config change was deployed 2026-03-11 03:10Z (PR linked).

Mitigation / temporary workarounds applied:
- Immediately routed BrightCart traffic to a dedicated serving pool (mitigates for this customer).
- Added a temporary router rule to avoid mixing high-length jobs with low-latency tenants in the same batch (limited roll-out to prod-us-east).

Work remaining / proposed fix:
- Short-term: implement tenant-aware batch composition heuristic that estimates per-request expected token cost and avoids coalescing requests with >3x length disparity. Target rollout: canary 2026-03-15.
- Mid-term: add adaptive per-tenant isolation thresholds in scheduler and expose policy via Console.
- Postmortem: analyze global traffic patterns to decide default behavior for shared pools and update docs/runbooks.

Requested from Eng/SRE:
- Confirm whether the router change on 2026-03-11 could alter batch composition behavior.
- Review serving-runtime kernel selection logs for affected batches and confirm whether long-request kernels caused amplified latency.

Customer note:
- BrightCart accepted dedicated-pool workaround and requested ETA on a permanent fix as this affects peak sale events.
